Although the physical illusion is separate from the spiritual power,

In support of this principle that Narayan (God himself) becomes Daridranarayan, they propose
That material power defeats God.
But Srila Jiva Goswami and Srila Vishwanath
Chakravarti Thakur presents a very beautiful example in its explanation. He says that although
the sun gives light everywhere, but clouds, darkness, and snowfall are all different parts of the sun. Without the sun,
there is no possibility of the sky being covered by clouds or darkness, nor can there be snowfall on the earth. Although life is sustained by the sun, darkness and snowfall produced by the sun
also disrupt life. But it is also a fact that the sun itself is never defeated by darkness,
clouds, or snowfall. The Sun is far away from such disturbances. Those who are ignorant, they
say that the sun is covered by clouds or darkness. Similarly, the Supreme Being, God, is always unaffected by the influence of material
power, although it is one of His powers. (Parasyashaktirvividhaiva)

Who misuse their little freedom. Vishnu Purana. According to Bhagavad Gita and other
All Vedic texts, all beings are produced by the power of Lord Kau Tatstha and in this way
They are always the power of God, not the mighty. All beings are like the rays of the sun.
As has been mentioned above, although there is no qualitative difference between the sun and its rays,
but sometimes the sun's rays are defeated by the other power of the sun, which is called cloud or snowfall. Similarly, although the living being is qualitatively one with the supreme power of God,
but they tend to be defeated by the inferior physical power. It is said in Vedic hymns
that all beings are like sparks of fire. The sparks of fire are also fire, but the burning power of the sparks
is different from the original fire. When the sphrigas break contact with the original fire and fly out,
they are affected by the fireless atmosphere. In this way, they maintain their power with fire in the form of sphriga,
but not in the form of the original fire.
These sparks can eternally remain within the original fire,
in a manner distinct from it, but the moment these sparks separate from the original fire,
then their misfortune and suffering begin. A clear conclusion emerged that God, who is
the original fire, is never defeated, but by the enchanting influence of the subtle sparks of fire,
they can be defeated. It is a very ridiculous argument to say that God is defeated by his own physical power.
God is the master of physical power, But living beings, in a bound state, are controlled by physical power. This is the statement of the Bhagavad Gita. Those Koopamanduka philosophers who present this argument
